methodologyNotes: This dataset covers thirteen high-search wearable, electric double, and portable breast pump models as of mid-2026. Primary sources are manufacturer product pages (elvie.com, onewillow.com, spectrababyusa.com, momcozy.com, babybuddhaproducts.com, pumpables.co) plus Target/Babylist/Save Rite Medical retail listings and authoritative review/clinical corroboration (BabyGearLab, WhichBreastPump, Lucie's List, Exclusive Pumping). Prices reflect publicly listed MSRP or current buy-now price in USD; boolean specs (rechargeable_battery, hospital_grade, closed_system) are true when the manufacturer or a medical review explicitly applies the label, false when explicitly denied, and null when neither confirmed nor denied. Weight is recorded per pump unit or motor (not packaging) in ounces, converted from manufacturer-stated grams where needed (1 g ≈ 0.0353 oz). All values independently re-verified 2026-06-19 against the cited primary/retail sources. accessedAt 2026-06-19.

products.name: Elvie Stride 2
products.priceNote: MSRP $269.99 on elvie.com (regular price; currently on sale at $202.49, 25% off). Elvie's Oct 29, 2024 PRNewswire launch release also states it "retails at $269.99".
products.provenance: Fetched elvie.com/products/elvie-stride-2 — confirmed as the exact model (page title "Elvie Stride 2: Hospital-Grade Suction Breast Pump"; an on-page FAQ explicitly contrasts Elvie Stride vs Stride 2), which states regular price $269.99 (sale $202.49), 10 intensity settings across Stimulation/Expression modes, up to -300 mmHg hospital-grade suction, and a rechargeable battery lasting nearly three hours. The breastpumpshub.com hands-on review corroborates a 270-300 mmHg hospital-grade range, closed system (prevents backflow), 10 intensity levels per mode, and a weight of 158 grams (5.6 oz) per cup. Model identity, the $269.99 US retail price, and an Oct 29, 2024 US launch are further confirmed by Elvie's PRNewswire press release (release recorded as 2024); type recorded as "wearable" since milk collects in hands-free in-bra cups, consistent with how the manufacturer and reviewers categorize it.

The Amazon listing (ASIN B0CYZLT7M2) corroborates the same model via Manufacturer Part Number T8D04121 (identical to the manufacturer URL, confirming it is the S1 Pro and not the S1/E10/E20 siblings), and adds verbatim "300 mmHg", "Noise Level 46 Decibels", "Battery Powered" with "1 Lithium Ion batteries required (included)", "Item Weight 9.12 ounces", and "Date First Available June 16, 2024". closed_system left null because neither page explicitly applies a "closed system" label (only "leakproof with a secure double seal"); weight_oz 9.12 is Amazon's stated item weight, and release 2024 is derived from Amazon's Date First Available.

products.priceNote: Cash/self-pay price $189.00 listed on the official motifmedical.com product page (the Luna is primarily offered through insurance). No price sourced from Amazon — the listing shows no featured offers/no buy price.
products.provenance: The official Motif Medical page (motifmedical.com/motif-luna-breast-pump) confirms this exact model, the "Motif Luna® Double Electric Breast Pump," stating a suction strength of 280 mmHg ("hospital-grade suction strength of up to 280 mmHg"), a closed system with backflow protection, a weight of "less than 2 pounds" (no exact figure, so weight_oz left null), and a listed cash price of $189.00; its FAQ explicitly states the Luna is "hospital strength... different from a hospital grade breast pump" (hospital_grade=false) and that the standard Luna "requires a wall outlet" (rechargeable_battery=false; a rechargeable battery is only in the separate "Luna with Battery" model). The Amazon listing (Model Number AAA0013) corroborates model identity as a double electric pump with closed-system backflow protection and "Power Source Corded Electric," but shows no featured offers, so the price is sourced solely from the manufacturer page. suction_levels and release are null because the pages describe cycle-per-minute speed settings rather than a discrete count of suction-intensity levels, and no release year is stated on either page.
